params.body:
3D was very laggy with every relation drawn. Measured on a demo copy with 733 relations and 1,623 lines (headless Chrome, software WebGL):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 3D draw calls per frame | 2,393 | 133 |
| 3D render time per frame | 14 to 23 ms | 1 ms |
| 3D frame rate once settled | 20 fps | 60 fps |
| 3D settle | 150 ticks | 70 ticks, from the flat picture's places |
| 2D first settle | 300 ticks, 10+ s | 200 ticks, 3.2 s |

**3D**
- The library draws only the relations that matter (not the small ones), opened projects, and the lines of the dot in focus, as plain lines (`linkWidth(0)`) instead of tubes.
- The small relations are one `THREE.Points` cloud and the resting lines one `THREE.LineSegments` with a colour per line; both are single draws, updated on each simulation tick (`move3d`).
- Hovering recolours and switches visibility; it no longer rebuilds every name sprite. The hovered dot's name is in the tooltip.
- The 3D modules are fetched while the page is idle, after the flat picture settles.

**Both views**
- `near()` uses a neighbour index built once per structure instead of scanning every line for every dot on every frame.
- The graph data and the graph instance are kept out of Alpine's reactivity (`__v_skip`), so the simulation's position updates are not tracked by a proxy.
- Faster alpha decay and fewer cooldown ticks.

`three` is now a direct dependency at `^0.186.1`, the version 3d-force-graph already installs (package.json and the lock's root entry only; nothing new is downloaded).

Most of the remaining time to open 3D in the headless check is creating a WebGL context in software (about 3 s there); the main thread was 81% idle while 3D settled.

Tests: 339 PHP tests and 19 JS tests pass. Checked by screenshot: 2D, 3D at rest, 3D with Gemeente Zulte in focus, no console errors.

params.title: Make the 3D network fast with every relation drawn
